label: Lucius - Medical History Import
info:
Manual/on-demand — not scheduled (PLAN.md §19). Watches /share/lucius_medical_history_import/ for *.yaml files matching the structured medical-history import format documented in PLAN.md §19, upserts one `cardiac`/`medical`-category incident per `encounters[]` entry via the new token-authenticated api/incident_push.php (idempotent on the YAML entry's `id` slug, stored as `incidents.external_ref`), then moves processed files into processed/.

Uses Node-RED's CORE `yaml` node to parse each file (no new dependency) — this is the first place this project's flows use it, so verify it against a real file in the editor before trusting it; see medical_history_import_test.json for the isolated check. Also the first place this project's flows use core `split`/`join` twice in sequence within one flow (once over the file list, once over the flattened encounters list) rather than nested — each pair fully resolves before the next begins, so this is NOT the trickier nested-parts case, but still worth confirming behaves as expected on first real run.

`symptom_context`/`therapy_history_reference`/`open_research_items` in the YAML are deliberately NOT read by this flow — per PLAN.md §19, those have no ingestible date (or aren't incident-shaped data at all) and stay reference-only in the file itself.

UNTESTED — built from the documented YAML schema and the proven api-token/upsert patterns used elsewhere in this project, but never run against a live file or a live GoDaddy endpoint.

name: Load secrets + start job log
Parse file list (empty = nothing to do)
Read this YAML file (msg.payload = filename)
comment: filenameType 'msg' reads msg.payload as the path — confirm this is still how your Node-RED version's file-in node reads a dynamic filename; several other flows in this project have hit palette-version schema drift on exactly this kind of "which msg property does the node actually read" question.

name: Extract encounters[] from this file
Join: wait for all files read
comment: Paired with n_mhi_split_files via msg.parts (mode: auto). Output is an array of arrays (one encounters[] array per file) — flattened by the next node, not itself.

name: Flatten to one encounters list
Build incident_push.php payload
Join: wait for all encounter pushes
comment: Paired with n_mhi_split_encounters via msg.parts (mode: auto). Sequential, not nested, relative to the files split/join above — that pair fully resolves before this one begins.

name: Tally results, prep processed/ move
Move processed files (msg.payload = full shell command)
Nothing to import this run
Log success + update HA status
Prepare finish-point write
Split entities for HA WebSocket node
Call HA service (set helper entity)
comment: Same node config as every other flow's equivalent — msg.payload carries {action, target, data} directly, UI Action/Targets/Data can stay blank. The one thing that must be set manually per install: the 'Server' field.

name: Catch any flow error (job_failed gap, Aug 2026)
comment: Fixes the gap flagged in PLAN.md §20's 'Known gap' note — this flow previously only handled its success path. Unlike body_comp_import_flow.json's exceljs-based job_failed (which wires from that node type's own native error output), nothing in this flow has a native error output — the `yaml` node and every `function` node here are single-output — so a real failure (malformed YAML, a bad file) needs a `catch` node to be caught at all. Scope null = catches any node on this tab, including node.error() calls like Load secrets' own JSON.parse failure.

name: Log failure + update HA status
